title: Stage-2 current-source load
description: The second-stage current-source load, drawn as a mirror output: one device on a bias reference's gate wire at a multiple of that reference's width, its drain at the output DC level. It is the device that sets the stage-2 current, and that current is read off the table at its own drain voltage rather than typed: the reference's current times the width ratio, scaled by what the difference between the two drain voltages does through its $g_{ds}$. Its output conductance loads the second-stage gain. A composing amplifier passes in the reference's width times its ratio, the reference's gate-source voltage and its length, maps the gate port onto the reference's gate wire, and hands the current this device delivers to the second-stage device. Used alone, the sheet sizes the device at the width and gate-source voltage typed here.

params.name: Wx
params.note: the device's width. A composing amplifier passes the bias reference's width times the mirror ratio, which is what makes this device a mirror output of that reference; the value here is only what the sheet sizes at alone, and as a width it means a different current on every table

params.name: vgsx
params.note: the gate-source voltage the device sits at: the level of its gate wire. A composing amplifier passes the bias reference's own gate-source voltage, the gate wire the two share; used alone, nothing on this sheet sets the gate, so it is a bias the designer applies

params.name: Lx
params.note: the device's length; a composing amplifier passes the reference's, because a mirror copies a current density at one length

params.name: vx
params.note: output DC level at this load's drain; sets the load's vds. The load is a current source at a high-impedance amplifier output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it, and a parent amplifier passes its own output level in
